stem.en: Flower P has sepals, petals and a pistil but no stamens. Flower Q, on another plant, has sepals, petals and stamens but no pistil. Which statement is correct?

text.en: P can form a fruit if pollen reaches its stigma

feedback.en: Yes. P has a pistil with ovules, but its pollen must come from another flower.

text.en: Q can form a fruit using its own pollen grains

feedback.en: Q has no pistil, so it has no stigma and no ovary. It cannot form a fruit.

text.en: Neither flower can have any part in reproduction

feedback.en: Each flower has a part to play. Q gives pollen and P receives it.

text.en: P makes the pollen that Q needs to form a fruit

feedback.en: Pollen comes from stamens, and P has none.

explanation.en: A fruit forms from the ovary of a pistil after pollen reaches the stigma. P has a pistil but needs pollen from another flower. Q can give pollen but cannot form a fruit.

hints.en: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
